object_types.name: Patient
object_types.definition: A person who books and attends appointments at the clinic.

source_references.excerpt: Patients book appointments. Every appointment is booked by exactly one patient, and a patient can have many appointments.
Patients have a patient ID -- it's on their card.

object_types.name: Doctor
object_types.definition: A clinician who sees patients in appointments and may be a patient's primary doctor.

source_references.excerpt: Each appointment is with exactly one doctor. Doctors see many patients across their appointments.
Doctors have a license number.

object_types.name: Appointment
object_types.definition: A scheduled visit between a patient and a doctor at a specific date and time slot.

source_references.excerpt: Appointments get an appointment number when they're created.

object_types.name: ExamRoom
object_types.definition: A physical room in the clinic used for exams.

source_references.excerpt: Exam rooms have a room number.

object_types.name: PatientId
object_types.definition: The identifying number on a patient's card.

source_references.excerpt: Patients have a patient ID -- it's on their card.

object_types.name: LicenseNumber
object_types.definition: The identifying license number of a doctor.

source_references.excerpt: Doctors have a license number.

object_types.name: AppointmentNumber
object_types.definition: The identifying number assigned to an appointment when created.

source_references.excerpt: Appointments get an appointment number when they're created.

object_types.name: RoomNumber
object_types.definition: The identifying number of an exam room.

source_references.excerpt: Exam rooms have a room number.

object_types.name: Specialty
object_types.definition: The medical specialty of a doctor, e.g. cardiology or general practice.

source_references.excerpt: Every doctor has exactly one specialty, like cardiology or general practice.

object_types.name: AppointmentDate
object_types.definition: The calendar date of an appointment.

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment is on a date and at a time slot

object_types.name: TimeSlot
object_types.definition: A fixed booking time slot such as 09:00 or 09:30.

source_references.excerpt: we book in fixed slots like 09:00 or 09:30

object_types.name: AppointmentStatus
object_types.definition: The current state of an appointment.

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment also has a status. The status is one of: scheduled, checked-in, completed, or cancelled.
An appointment always has exactly one status from that list.

object_types.name: VisitReason
object_types.definition: The reason for the visit given by the patient at booking time.

source_references.excerpt: An appointment can have a visit reason the patient gives when booking

object_types.name: FollowUpNote
object_types.definition: A note attached by the doctor after the visit.

source_references.excerpt: after the visit the doctor can attach a follow-up note. At most one follow-up note per appointment.

ambiguities.description: ExamRoom is mentioned only with an identifier (room number) but no relationship to Appointment, Doctor, or Patient is described. Should appointments be linked to exam rooms, and if so, what is the cardinality (one room per appointment, one appointment per room per time slot)?

ambiguities.description: VisitReason is described as optional ('can have'), but it's unclear whether a visit reason, once given, is unique to that appointment only or could be reused/shared text across appointments -- this affects whether it should be modeled as a value type or something more structured. Also unclear if it's truly free text or from a limited set.

ambiguities.description: The relationship between primary doctor and appointment doctor is stated as 'separate', but it's not clarified whether a patient's appointments must ever involve their primary doctor, or whether the primary doctor assignment can change over time (temporal tracking not addressed).
